78550.subject: Fomo Goes Parabolic
78550.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Gm, and happy Friday! 

The macroeconomic backdrop is flashing warning signs, and institutional capital is taking notice. ETF buyers are accelerating purchases of both Bitcoin and Gold ETFs as investors seek refuge from a cornered Fed. Plus, we break down the parabolic rise of Fomo, a social trading app pulling in over $13M in monthly revenue that may be crypto's breakout consumer application. 

Let’s get into it.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Grouping daily ETF flows into regimes by the sign of trailing 30-day flow shows the turn began earlier than price did. The distribution phase that ran from May 20 through July 29 drained ~88.5k BTC (the deepest of the past year) before flipping to accumulation on July 30. This regime has now pulled in ~53k BTC in roughly five weeks, nearly matching the ~48k BTC accumulated across the ten-week spring phase and at more than twice the rate. Notably, the regime turned three weeks before BTC broke out on August 19, so ETF demand led the price move rather than chasing it. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cce48fe0-ee69-4eca-8ffb-ab3a5a5d3729/image.png?t=1788527474)
Caption: 

An explanation for the return of demand is that BTC is trading as part of a broader monetary hedge, and the flow data offers some evidence for it. Net flows into gold and Bitcoin ETFs have broadly trended in the same direction. While gold and BTC often diverge, their correlation has now reached a 6-year high (after the monetary stimulus for COVID). 

Both series bottomed within weeks of each other in mid-2026 and are recovering in tandem, with running totals since launch back near $55B for BTC and $50B for gold. With inflation above target, debt issuance expanding and long-term borrowing costs elevated, portfolios can allocate to both a traditional safe haven and a risk asset since both express the same view on the monetary environment. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/655bb1fe-7f06-4da1-8698-1b343039a69f/image.png?t=1788527474)
Caption: 

This is happening as the monetary backdrop has grown less favorable over the past month. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.79% on September 1, up from 4.28% a year earlier and 82bp off its February low of 3.97%. The move is global as rates in Europe are also on the rise and Japan's 10-year yield crossed 3% for

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk appetite roared back after a dovish nudge from the Fed pushed Bitcoin above $81,000 and torched over $415M in shorts. Beneath the rally, Washington's crypto agenda wobbles and sanctioned hackers keep probing DeFi's plumbing. 🚀 Bitcoin Reclaims $81K as Fed's Waller Signals Rate Pause Bitcoin surged nearly 6% to top $81,000 for the first time since May after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he could support holding rates steady this month. The dovish tilt cut September hike odds from roughly 63% to about 50%, dragged the dollar index below 99, and triggered a short squeeze that liquidated more than $415 million in bearish bets. Ether, XRP and BNB rallied alongside as risk appetite returned. A 60-day public comment window opens once the rule hits the Federal Register. More details → 🏛️ Clarity Act on Life Support as Senate Vote Looms Crypto's flagship market-structure bill, the Clarity Act, enters September with slim odds of passing, and many industry insiders are now resigned that it is dead for 2026. The bill would split oversight between the SEC and CFTC and set registration and anti-money-laundering requirements. Even if it fails, executives note the SEC, CFTC and OCC have already turned markedly friendlier under Trump. Dear professionals, we are pleased to share the August edition of the PFI Monthly Research Report. This issue explores key themes shaping financial markets, corporate finance, Czech M&A and private equity — with a common thread running through it: the growing gap between compelling stories and disciplined investment returns. In this issue, we have prepared for you: • PFI Monthly research report including an interview with Julia Cillikova, Executive Director Supervision and Financial Consumer Protection Department at National Bank of Slovakia • Financial markets – The AI boom through the lens of capital cycle theory, arguing that high returns attract capital until new capacity erodes margins; a case that 60/40 is not a neutral allocation but an implicit bet on the inflation regime; an analysis of the S&P 500’s Shiller CAPE reaching 41.18, its second-highest reading in ~155 years; and why the 10-year US Treasury yield has risen toward 4.7% as US government debt surpasses USD 40tn. • Corporate finance – Capital allocation 101 (Part I): a clear map of where corporate capital comes from and the main routes to deploy it — organic investment, M&A, buybacks and dividends — and why each choice creates or destroys value. • Czech M&A – Pekárny Srnín’s agreed acquisition of PAC Hořovice, a transaction implying a value of around CZK 1bn that would mark the largest Czech bakery deal since 2019 and accelerate sector consolidation. • Private equity – Building beats buying: add-on acquisitions now account for roughly three-quarters of US buyout activity, making operational integration — not deal access — the real differentiator. 👉 Read the full edition to explore all insights in detail. We would also like to warmly thank partners of the Prague Finance Institute: CERGE-EI, Deník e15, KPMG Czech Republic, Conseq Investment Management, a.s., Oriens, PPF Group, TARPAN Partners, BHM group, RSJ Investments, ARETE, X Production s.r.o., White & Case LLP, Cushman & Wakefield, House of Julius Meinl Limited, Datasite and EKP Advisory. Welcome back! Today: Nvidia funding its own customers, OpenAI's agent that uses software like a person, a forecasting model that needs no training and ChatGPT, Claude and Grok all offline at once In today's Atlas Newsletter: Who funds Nvidia's customers? Nvidia may put $2.5 billion into Thinking Machines Lab, which has already committed to a gigawatt of Nvidia infrastructure. What happens when AI stops needing an API? GPT-6 Astra uses the same screens your employees use, from CRM records to CAD tools. Can one model forecast anything? Google's TimesFM-3 makes zero-shot predictions across interconnected signals, with no per-dataset training. What happens when three rivals share one dependency? ChatGPT, Claude and Grok all went down Thursday morning, and the common thread points somewhere boring. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions Nvidia is funding the companies that buy its chips Nvidia may invest $2.5 billion in Thinking Machines Lab, the AI startup founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati. The startup is also reportedly raising at least $1 billion at a valuation of around $40 billion. The detail that explains the deal: Thinking Machines Lab has already committed to using at least 1 gigawatt of Nvidia's Vera Rubin infrastructure. So Nvidia could invest in the company, and part of that money may eventually come back to Nvidia through hardware purchases. This isn't new. Nvidia has made similar investments in OpenAI, Anthropic, cloud companies and AI infrastructure startups. It has backed more than 100 startups in the past two years. The strategy is simple: Nvidia needs AI companies to keep buying more compute, so investing in them helps secure future demand for its chips. The concern is circularity. If Nvidia invests in a company that then spends heavily on Nvidia hardware, it becomes harder to tell how much demand is truly independent. And Nvidia is spending aggressively across the AI ecosystem, including the reported $12.93 billion Hugging Face acquisition and the $1 billion Poolside deal. Nvidia now sells the infrastructure behind AI and funds the companies that need it. The enterprise deal is ready. Is your SOC 2?
